The Started Advisory Board Brings FinTech Leaders Together for Candid AI Debate
summary:
As excitement and concern around AI grow in equal measure, the Started Advisory Board convened CEOs, founders and financial services leaders for a behind-closed-doors discussion on accountability, trust and what the sector cannot afford to get wrong.
On Thursday 15 October, the Started Advisory Board, a unique fintech communications-focused think tank, brought together senior leaders from fintech, banking, payments, investment and media for an open debate on AI, accountability and trust in financial services. 
Curated by Started PR, and hosted by Checkout.com, An Evening with the Started Advisory Board explored how financial services businesses can realise AI’s benefits while retaining human judgement, clear accountability and customer trust. An audience open mic invited guests to challenge the panel, share experiences and question assumptions about how AI will shape the sector. 
The evening opened with remarks from Asif Faruque, Senior Director of Communications at Checkout.com, before a live debate hosted by author and presenter Ian Horne. Contributors included Advisory Board members Susanne Chishti, Katie Ramsey, Jas Shah, Raf De Kimpe, Jason Williams and David Savage. The event brought together a high-calibre audience of CEOs, founders, operators and those building the next generation of financial services in the age of AI. 
The debate explored the gap between AI’s promise and its practical value, the balance between innovation and accountability, and the implications for jobs, skills and customer trust. Panellists and audience members questioned whether faster output means better outcomes, where human judgement must remain central and how businesses can encourage experimentation while managing risk. 
Fintech Product Consultant Jas Shah said: “The perception of how much AI is transforming financial institutions is far from the reality. I think people are talking more about what they’re doing with AI than actually doing it. The human element is still very important: understanding the processes, understanding the value your company offers and feeding that into a process AI can use to create value.” 
The conversation also explored the tension between encouraging experimentation and controlling “shadow AI”, where employees use tools outside approved systems. Contributors called for clear, regularly reviewed policies, effective tools and a culture where employees can learn without fear of failure. They also questioned whether restrictive policies push experimentation out of sight, increasing risks around confidential data and oversight. 
Founder and Chair of FINTECH Circle Susanne Chishti said: “It’s a fine balance. You want everybody to use AI as much as possible, but within guardrails, especially in a regulated financial services company. Having humans in control is very important but they can become the bottleneck. As AI enabled work is faster to produce, it creates more work to check it. Working with AI is powerful and fun, but it doesn’t necessarily give you the free time you initially expected as you find new AI applications which you want to pursue to get things done.”
The evening highlighted the continuing value of distinctive expertise, personal relationships and face-to-face discussion. Contributors argued that credibility and trust will become more valuable as AI makes content and other outputs easier to produce, placing greater importance on original perspectives, strong networks and the exchange of ideas in person. 
The Started Advisory Board brings together founders, investors, operators and industry commentators to inform Started PR’s work and give clients access to expertise and relationships across financial services. Its members are David M. Brear, Jason Mikula, Sarah Kocianski, David Savage, Jas Shah, Jason Williams, Monica Millares, Raf De Kimpe, Susanne Chishti and Katie Ramsey. 
Kimberley Waldron, Chair of the Started Advisory Board and Managing Director of Started PR, said: “Our Advisory Board and wider network brought real experience and challenge to this important industry debate. As our panel discussed, AI is creating huge opportunities, but human judgement, accountability and trust remain essential. Thank you to Checkout.com for hosting a candid conversation about what financial services needs to get right.”

TreviPay Expands Pay by Invoice Availability for Walmart Business Customers
summary:
TreviPay, a global B2B payments infrastructure partner, today announced the general availability of Pay By Invoice for eligible Walmart Business customers. Following an initial pilot, the expanded availability gives more organizations a new way to manage purchasing and payments online and in Walmart stores. Walmart Business Pay By Invoice provides net 30-day terms, a dedicated business line of credit and detailed invoicing built into the Walmart Business purchasing experience.
Powered by TreviPay, Walmart Business Pay By Invoice is designed to give organizations greater flexibility in how they manage business purchases and payments. Eligible customers can get what they need and pay on net 30-day terms, helping them preserve cash flow for other priorities while keeping operations moving. Purchasing controls and payment reconciliation also help organizations share purchasing responsibilities while maintaining oversight and keeping purchase activity, invoices, payments, returns and refunds organized in one place.
“Retailers have a significant opportunity to build stronger relationships with business buyers by recognizing that their purchasing needs are different from those of consumers,” said Brandon Spear, CEO of TreviPay. “Business buyers need payment choice, purchasing controls and terms that align with how their organizations manage cash flow. When retailers make those capabilities part of the purchasing experience, they make it easier for business customers to buy from them and come back again and again.”
The general availability follows an initial rollout of the TreviPay-powered solution. During that period, Walmart Business customers reported a 90% customer satisfaction score with the program. The results reinforce the value of giving business customers greater flexibility and control over how they purchase and pay. Pay By Invoice can support organizations with complex purchasing and recordkeeping needs such as:
Schools, colleges and universities can centralize purchasing records across departments or campuses to support budgeting, compliance requirements and audit preparation.
Nonprofits can organize purchasing across programs, events or grant-funded initiatives, while government agencies and public sector organizations can maintain purchasing and payment records to support procurement, financial reporting, compliance and audits.
Businesses can purchase inventory and supplies but enjoy 30 days to pay, thereby preserving cash flow for other expenses, and purchasing controls helping owners and managers share buying responsibilities while maintaining oversight.

Nutanix Builds a Faster Foundation for Production AI
summary:
Nutanix, a hybrid cloud leader and AI platform company, today announced it is collaborating with NVIDIA, Supermicro, and Netris to deliver new AI solutions that aim to simplify the infrastructure required for production AI and help organisations bring new capabilities online faster. By combining Nutanix software with leading hardware, networking, and silicon technologies, Nutanix aims to help enterprises deploy and operate production AI environments more efficiently at scale. 
As organisations push more AI workloads into production, capacity constraints and operational complexity can make it harder to move quickly.  Nutanix and its partners are working to simplify that path to make it easier to bring AI into production faster and accelerate time to value.
“Organisations need more than just advanced infrastructure to move agentic AI into production – we believe they need an AI cloud that simply connects intelligence, agents, enterprise applications, and data across CPUs, GPUs, virtual machines, containers, on-premises environments, and cloud,” said Thomas Cornely, Executive Vice President, Product Management at Nutanix. “Through our collaboration with NVIDIA, Supermicro, and Netris, we plan to help customers accelerate deployments of agents and AI services on a unified platform with built-in security, performance, and governance.” 
Extending Agentic AI to the CPU Layer with NVIDIA Vera 
As enterprises adopt agentic AI at scale, they are anticipated to require infrastructure that can support increasingly demanding workloads across the full AI environment, not just GPU-intensive tasks. Agentic applications combine inference with tool calls, code execution, retrieval, orchestration, and outcome processing. As these workflows scale, CPU performance is expected to become essential for completing the steps between GPU operations, reducing delays, and maximising overall AI-factory efficiency. To help ensure this critical compute path does not become a bottleneck, Nutanix plans to work towards Day Zero support for NVIDIA Vera CPUs, beginning with NKP Bare Metal, to serve highly performance-sensitive AI factory environments, with planned expansion to virtualised Nutanix environments.
By pairing NVIDIA’s purpose-built CPU architecture – engineered for high-speed agent execution and reduced latency – and NVIDIA OpenShell  to create safe, private runtime environments for agents with NKP, the collaboration aims to give organisations a predictable, high-performance foundation for their most advanced AI agents. 
This support is expected to give organisations greater flexibility in how they safely deploy agentic AI while simplifying operations with a consistent cloud operating model.
Nutanix and Supermicro Take on Runaway AI Costs with Jointly Engineered System for Private Inference  
Nutanix and Supermicro are announcing plans for a jointly engineered AI infrastructure solution built around validated Supermicro server systems. By combining Supermicro servers and NVIDIA GPUs with Nutanix Agentic AI (NAI) and NVIDIA Spectrum-XTM Ethernet networking, the solution is being designed to help reduce custom configuration and integration delays, with the goal of helping enterprises get on-premises GPU capacity and take on runaway AI costs with a jointly engineered system powered by NAI for private inference.
As AI requirements grow, the architecture is expected to  be able to scale GPU capacity to meet evolving requirements. Nutanix provides an AI cloud control plane and AI storage purpose-built to  support workloads with resilient operations and high-throughput data workflows. Customers are anticipated to gain a predictable path to deploy, manage, and scale AI inference workloads without assembling and integrating a complex, multivendor environment.
Nutanix and Netris: Making Multitenant AI Infrastructure Easier to Deploy and Operate
For NVIDIA Cloud Partner reference architectures, multitenancy is designed to extend across AI infrastructure, including the physical network.  In dynamic neocloud environments, operators also must be able to automate network access and ensure  tenant isolation as customers, workloads, and GPU allocations change.  Nutanix and Netris are collaborating to automate this network-layer multitenancy and turn complex GPU infrastructure into secure, cloud-like, multitenant AI services.
Nutanix will provide the foundation for compute across virtual machines, containers, CPUs, and GPUs, along with storage, security, Kubernetes, and Nutanix Agent Gateway, model-as-a-service and AI platform services. Netris will provide network automation, abstraction, and multitenancy across the physical network fabric, with hard isolation (enforced on networking hardware) from compute through the physical network. Together, the integrated solution will provide a cloud-like self-service operating experience across bare-metal and virtualised AI infrastructure, helping providers instantly onboard tenants and deliver AI services more efficiently.
Analyst Commentary
“Nutanix built its enterprise business by simplifying virtualised infrastructure and more recently containerised workloads," said Don Gentile, Analyst, Data Platforms and Resiliency, HyperFRAME Research. "Now it's extending that expertise to bare- metal AI systems, agent execution, private inference, and multitenant cloud services. Through innovation and targeted partnerships, Nutanix is advancing a common cloud operating model that enterprises and service providers have long wanted: consistent management, automation, and choice across increasingly diverse infrastructure.”
Ecosystem Commentary
“AI agents need fast CPUs to execute code, use tools and process data between model calls,” said Hannah Coutand, Director of Product Marketing for Vera CPU at NVIDIA. “NVIDIA Vera is purpose-built for this work, and our collaboration with Nutanix will help enterprises bring high-performance agentic AI into production with a consistent cloud operating model.”
Customer Commentary
“Digital and AI transformation is a fundamental pillar supporting the Kingdom’s ambitions to build cutting-edge, resilient, agile, and data-driven public services. Through our collaboration with Nutanix, we look forward to exploring how Nutanix’s platform for hybrid cloud computing across multiple environments can support the adoption of AI technologies and help develop national capabilities in advanced cloud and AI technologies.”
– Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA) - Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
